newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Shenzhen sees net cash withdrawal in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China's Shenzhen sees net cash withdrawal in 1996.

text.p: China's southern boomtown of Shenzhen withdrew a net 7.0 billion yuan ($840 million) of cash from circulation in 1996, according to figures from the city branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
"This is one indication that the financial sector of our city is in good condition," the official Xinhua news agency on Thursday quoted a bank official as saying.
The banking system extended 101.1 billion yuan and recalled 83.6 billion yuan in loans last year, he said.
Outstanding deposits stood at 154.5 billion yuan at the end of the year, up 28 percent, while loans were 96.7 billion yuan at the year-end, up 22 percent, he said.
Outstanding hard currency deposits at Chinese banks rose by $106 million to $6.5 billion, while outstanding foreign exchange loans were up $780 million to $6.4 billion, he said.
The value insured in 1996 exceeded 500 billion yuan.
Overseas financial institutions numbered 54 by year-end and of these 27 were operational. Their outstanding deposits stood at $750 million while loans totalled $3.7 billion, he said.
